findings.evidence: "The stipend clock resumes on their first day back."
findings.fix: Replace "stipend clock" with the specific mechanism it refers to (e.g., "the 90-day service requirement" or "the benefit-year eligibility window").
findings.location: Eligibility, paragraph on leave of absence
findings.violation: "Stipend clock" is never defined anywhere in the document, so it's unclear whether this refers to the 90-day service requirement, the benefit-year claim window, or something else.

findings.evidence: "The summary shows the equipment cost and the requested delivery date."
findings.fix: Either remove "requested delivery date" or clarify whether this stipend involves company-ordered equipment in addition to reimbursement.
findings.violation: The rest of the policy describes a reimbursement model (employee purchases equipment, submits a receipt, and is reimbursed), but this line implies the company is shipping equipment directly to the employee, which contradicts that model.

findings.evidence: "an incomplete request pauses the timeline until the missing item arrives"
findings.fix: Reword to specify what is missing, e.g., "until the employee submits the missing information."
findings.violation: "Missing item" is ambiguous - it could mean a missing document/field in the request or a missing physical piece of equipment, and the surrounding context doesn't disambiguate.

findings.evidence: "A photo of the receipt is enough for most requests."
findings.fix: Either specify what the exceptions are and what documentation they require, or remove "most" if a photo receipt is always sufficient.
findings.violation: "Most requests" implies there are exceptions requiring something more, but no exception or additional requirement is ever described.

findings.evidence: "You must keep your equipment in good working condition and we may ask for a brief photo check once a year."
findings.fix: Rewrite in third person, e.g., "Employees must keep equipment in good working condition, and the benefits team may request a brief photo check once a year."
findings.violation: This sentence switches to second-person ("You"/"we") while every other section of the policy uses third person ("Employees," "The manager," "The finance office"), creating an inconsistent voice.

findings.evidence: "Similarly, the policy applies to one device per category per employee."
findings.fix: Replace "Similarly" with a neutral transition like "Additionally" or move this sentence to a more relevant section (e.g., Eligibility).
findings.violation: "Similarly" implies a logical parallel to the previous sentence about photo checks, but a one-device-per-category limit is an unrelated rule, making the transition illogical.

findings.evidence: "Finance reconciles the stipend item against the request log each month."
findings.fix: Rename the section to reflect its actual content (e.g., "Monthly Reconciliation Process"), and either define "request log" or replace it with "reimbursement log" if they are the same thing.
findings.violation: The section is titled "Terminology Notes" but contains no term definitions, only process narrative, and it introduces "request log" - a term not used or defined anywhere else (it's unclear if this is the same as the "reimbursement log" mentioned in Program Overview).

findings.evidence: "Payroll releases the stipend item amount after that monthly review" (Terminology Notes); "The finance office deposits the amount within one pay cycle" (Reimbursement Amounts); "the team schedules the reimbursement for the next pay cycle" (Program Coordination)
findings.fix: Consolidate into a single disbursement description with one responsible party and one timeline, stated once and referenced elsewhere if needed.
findings.location: Terminology Notes vs. Reimbursement Amounts vs. Program Coordination
findings.violation: Three different sections give three different, mutually inconsistent accounts of who disburses the stipend (finance office vs. payroll vs. benefits team) and when (within one pay cycle vs. after a monthly review vs. next pay cycle).

findings.evidence: "Also, you submit the request in the portal. You track its status there until the payment clears."
findings.fix: Remove this redundant paragraph or merge its content into "How to Apply" using third-person phrasing.
findings.violation: Another shift to second person, inconsistent with the rest of the document, and this content duplicates what's already stated in "How to Apply" and "Program Coordination."

findings.evidence: "Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and uploading the receipt."
findings.fix: Clarify the actual step order across the whole document and either merge "Request Steps" into "How to Apply" or correct the sequence so receipt upload happens after purchase/approval.
findings.violation: This single-sentence section implies the receipt is uploaded at the very start of the request, before the manager approval described in "Approval Timeline," which contradicts the implied purchase-then-reimburse sequence (you can't have a purchase receipt before the request is even approved). It also duplicates "How to Apply" with a different, conflicting step order.

findings.evidence: "The finance liaison publishes the equipment catalog at the start of the fiscal year." (Special Cases) vs. "the IT asset group tracks the equipment catalog on the first business day of the month." (Program Overview)
findings.fix: State ownership and update cadence for the equipment catalog once, in one section, and remove the conflicting claim.
findings.violation: These two sections contradict each other on who maintains the equipment catalog (finance liaison vs. IT asset group) and how often it's updated (fiscal-year start vs. monthly).

findings.evidence: "The finance office reviews every stipend request over 200 dollars before it pays out."
findings.fix: Integrate this threshold into "Approval Timeline" so the full approval sequence (manager review, then finance review if applicable) is described in one place.
findings.violation: This introduces a new $200 review threshold and approval step that isn't mentioned in "Approval Timeline," leaving it unclear how this review relates to (or sequences with) the manager's two-business-day review.

findings.evidence: "The finance office also flags any request that repeats within the same quarter."
findings.fix: Clarify whether multiple claims per year are actually possible under some circumstance, or remove this sentence as redundant/contradictory with the one-claim-per-year rule.
findings.violation: This contradicts Eligibility's statement that the stipend covers "one claim per employee per benefit year" - if only one claim per year is allowed, a repeat claim within the same quarter should already be rejected outright, not merely flagged.

findings.evidence: "The benefits team reviews the equipment catalog at the start of the fiscal year."
findings.fix: Remove the duplicate claims and state catalog ownership and review cadence exactly once.
findings.location: Questions and Updates vs. Special Cases/Program Overview
findings.violation: This is a third conflicting claim about who is responsible for the equipment catalog (benefits team here, finance liaison in Special Cases, IT asset group in Program Overview), compounding the earlier contradiction.

findings.evidence: "Staff can request a printed copy from the benefits team at any time."
findings.fix: Specify what the printed copy is of, e.g., "a printed copy of the equipment catalog."
findings.violation: "A printed copy" has no clear antecedent in this sentence - it's not explicit whether it refers to the equipment catalog, the policy itself, or something else.
